title: Roulette (new finding: heal branch ends the whole attack)
problem: The 50% roll is made per hit inside the hit loop, but when it lands on "heal" the code exits the whole attack routine. With extra attacks ("attacks N additional times") every later hit is lost: it neither deals damage nor heals. The after-attack steps are skipped as well (Invisible removal, Prejudice, Spooky Technique). Text: each time it attacks, 50% heal, otherwise 50% more damage.
notes: Text: When this creature {ACTION_attacks}, it has a 50% chance to deal no damage and heal all your creatures for the amount of damage it would have dealt. Otherwise, it deals 50% more damage. Evidence: bc_CreatureAttack hit loop L1076-L1892 (increment/continue block @0x1406d0568, back edge @0x1406f6748). Roulette L1742-L1776 is inside it: L1775 dmg ([rsp+0x350]) = 0, L1776 `jmp 0x1406f957d` @0x1406f09b2 = function epilogue (return). dmg is recomputed for each hit at L1142. Fix sketch: Byte edit at 0x1406f09b2: change `jmp 0x1406f957d` (e9 c6 8b 00 00) to `jmp 0x1406d0568` (e9 b1 fb fd ff), i.e. continue with the next hit instead of returning. dmg is zeroed at L1775 and recomputed at L1142; after the last hit the normal post-loop phase (L1893-L1960) runs. Reasoning: The roll is per hit, so the text's 50/50 applies to each attack; the early return silently deletes the remaining attacks. Retargeting the jump to the loop's own continue block is the smallest change and is the same path as the normal back edge. App note (unpatched game): In the unpatched game, when Roulette heals, the rest of that attack (its remaining extra hits) is cancelled. Source: errata round 2 (2026-10-26). | Patched (batch M, 2026-10-26): byte edit in bc_CreatureAttack L1776 @0x1406f09b2: `jmp 0x1406f957d` (function exit) -> `jmp 0x1406d0568` (the hit loop's own continue block, the target of its back edge @0x1406f6748). dmg was set to 0 at L1775 and is recomputed per hit at L1142; after the last hit the post-loop phase (L1893+) runs as for a normal attack. Checked: no non-volatile register is written anywhere in the loop body, so the shorter path leaves no register state behind. | 2026-10-26 in-game crash (user, heavy group off): GML 'STRING argument is unset' at bc_CreatureAttack L1076 (the hit-loop test `i <= hits`), reached through this patch's jump from the L1776 heal branch into the loop's continue block: the heal branch does not keep the loop state valid for another pass. Default off (status needs-hook) until the continuation is rebuilt with the loop state restored. | Rebuilt (batch M, 2026-10-26; group heavy, default on) after the in-game crash. Root cause of the crash: the return tail of the heal branch is SHARED. L1776 is `store return value (0x1406f0992-0x1406f09aa); jmp epilogue (0x1406f09b2)`, and the pre-loop L176 exit (Stomp, trait 508: 'Attack failed (Stomp)') jumps into that same tail at 0x1406f09a2 (jmp @0x1406a7ef9). The first build retargeted the shared jmp @0x1406f09b2 to the hit loop's continue block, so every Stomp-interrupted attack entered the hit loop before L1076 had set i ([rsp+0x730], still the prologue's unset value): the ++ helper (0x14028c590) has no case for an unset value and its error formatter converts the operand to text (0x147874620), which raises 'STRING argument is unset' -> bc_CreatureAttack L1076. The second report ('Cannot compare unset variables', bc_CreatureAttack L38 attacker.resistant, from bc_OnDeath / Ceaseless Fighting) is not explained by the code statically; it reads an attacker instance without that variable and may be a follow-on of continuing past the first error. New edit: the 8-byte L1776 line marker @0x1406f098a (`mov dword [rsp+0x40], 0x6f0`, reached only by fallthrough from L1775 dmg = 0, whose only entries are the L1763 heal loop's exits) -> `jmp stub; nop x3`. The shared tail 0x1406f09a2-0x1406f09b6 is untouched, so the L176 exit returns exactly as before. Stub @0x149856760 (117 bytes): an instruction-for-instruction replica of L1789 (attacker.first_attack_done = true via varset, as every hit runs it, dodged or not), then `jmp 0x1406f4cb3` = L1871, the point a dodged hit reaches (the false target of L1834 `if !dodged || still_hits`). So the heal hit skips the dodge branch (L1791-L1827: no 'dodged' history, no bc_OnDodge) and the damage event (L1834-L1870), runs the per-hit end once (L1871-L1892: perks 512 / 509 / 510 / 497 follow-ups, same as a dodged hit), takes the back edge (L1892 -> L1076: i++ and the i <= hits test with i and hits set), and after the last hit the post-loop phase (L1893-L1960: Prejudice, Spooky Technique, Chastity, Invisible removal) runs normally. Builder asserts: site bytes/marker values (L1775, L1776, L1789, L1834, L1871); every jump into [L1775, tail) comes from the Roulette block and targets L1775; the only foreign entry is Stomp's into the tail; the Roulette block is only entered from inside the hit loop; no other patch edits or branches into L1775-L1776 or the tail; flags dead at L1871; no non-volatile register (rbx/rsi/rdi/rbp/r12-r15, xmm6-15) is written anywhere in the loop; at L1871 every register is written before it is read; stack-slot audit in both directions: every slot the heal branch or the skipped L1791-L1870 writes is, in the code that now runs after it (L1871-L1892, the post-loop phase, and the next hit L1076-L1741), first written again (locals) or first released by the temp release pattern (temps 0x48 / 0x58 / 0xa8 / 0x1b8), or is an argument-array entry; the stub replica decodes to the same instructions and targets as L1789. tools/skip_audit.py logic on the edit: 0 slots to check. SU-0039 (L1780 constant @0x1406f13e9, the other branch) is unaffected. In-game test: give a creature Roulette and several attacks per turn (e.g. 'attacks N additional times' traits, Quadhits, Die, Die, Die!) and attack repeatedly: on a heal roll the hit shows no damage and your creatures are healed, then the remaining hits continue (each one a fresh 50/50) and the after-attack effects (Prejudice, Spooky Technique, Invisible removal) happen; also have a creature with Stomp in your party and let enemies attack (35% of their attacks are interrupted): an interrupted attack just fails ('Attack failed (Stomp)'), no crash (this exit shares the return code the first build had redirected).

release_notes.intended: When this creature attacks, it has a 50% chance to deal no damage and heal all your creatures for the amount of damage it would have dealt. Otherwise, it deals 50% more damage.
release_notes.actual: In the unpatched game, a successful heal roll ended the whole attack: a creature that attacks several times lost all its remaining hits (they neither dealt damage nor healed), and the effects that happen after an attack (such as Prejudice, Spooky Technique and losing Invisible) did not happen.
release_notes.fix: Now a heal roll only replaces that one hit: it deals no damage and heals your creatures, and the hit then ends like any hit that dealt no damage (effects that trigger after each hit still happen). The creature carries on with its remaining hits, each rolling Roulette again, and the after-attack effects happen as usual.
